clippings.speaker: Billy Wilder
clippings.quote: We meet at, say, 9:30 in the morning and open shop, like bank tellers, and we sit there in one room … Sometimes nothing happens. Sometimes it goes on until 12:30, and then I’ll ask him, “How about a drink?’’ And he nods, and then we have a drink and go to lunch.
clippings.title: Conversations with Billy Wilder & I.A.L. Diamond [Part 1]
clippings.context: Joint seminar-style interview (c. 1976, original publication unnamed) excerpted by Scott Myers; Wilder describing their daily routine.

clippings.speaker: Billy Wilder
clippings.quote: Oh, he collaborates with me all the time. He just doesn’t get the credit for it.
clippings.title: Conversations with Billy Wilder & I.A.L. Diamond [Part 4]
clippings.context: Same joint interview; Wilder jumping in when Diamond was asked whether he ever collaborated on the direction.

clippings.speaker: I. A. L. Diamond
clippings.quote: No, we don’t co-direct. I may sit on the sidelines, and I may make a suggestion occasionally, but I stay out.
clippings.title: Conversations with Billy Wilder & I.A.L. Diamond [Part 4]
clippings.context: Same joint interview; Diamond's answer, right after Wilder said he collaborates on the direction without credit.

clippings.speaker: I. A. L. Diamond
clippings.quote: Oh, I throw out ideas, and sometimes they’re listened to and sometimes they’re not.
clippings.title: Conversations with Billy Wilder & I.A.L. Diamond [Part 4]
clippings.context: Same joint interview; asked how involved he gets in casting and other matters once the script is done.

clippings.speaker: Billy Wilder
clippings.quote: Then I heard Diamond say, “Nobody’s perfect.” I thought about it and I said, Well, let’s put in “Nobody’s perfect” for now. But only for the time being. … When we screened the movie, that line got one of the biggest laughs I’ve ever heard in the theater.
clippings.title: Written Interview: Billy Wilder [The Paris Review]
clippings.context: James Linville's Spring 1996 Paris Review interview, excerpted on Go Into The Story; on writing the film's final line.

clippings.speaker: Billy Wilder
clippings.quote: We never talked about personal things. That was the beauty of it. … But Iz Diamond was a very taciturn guy, my partner. It was wonderful to talk about dialogue, or about structure. He was always on the set with me.
clippings.title: Seven Things to Know About I.A.L. Diamond
clippings.context: From Cameron Crowe's Vanity Fair interview with Wilder (later in Conversations with Wilder), as quoted by the blog.

clippings.speaker: Billy Wilder
clippings.quote: If I ever lost this guy, I'd be like Abercrombie without Fitch.
clippings.title: I.A.L. Diamond, the Oscar-winning writer whose 30-year association with...
clippings.context: Earlier Wilder remark recalled in UPI's obituary of Diamond.

clippings.speaker: I. A. L. Diamond
clippings.quote: Billy … is a writer who is also a director.
clippings.title: The Beginning of a Beautiful Affair Between Billy Wilder and I.A.L. Diamond
clippings.context: Asked by the Los Angeles Times who mattered most, writer, actor or director, Diamond chose the writer, then made Wilder the exception; quoted by PopMatters, original date unknown.

notes: Diamond's own words about Wilder are scarce (he died 1988; his 1986 AFI tribute is video only). The joint interview's original publication (likely a c. 1976 AFI seminar) is unnamed by the host; UPI and Paris Review blocked curl, UPI line confirmed via WebFetch.
